rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes exposing carbon steels with varying Cr content to simulated environments, while the target study deposited an AlCoCrFeNi HEA coating on SS316L via APS and annealed it. These are fundamentally different interventions (composition variation vs. coating).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis mentions moderate to high temperatures (~300°C), pressurized water, and controlled chemical exposures, whereas the target used 3.5 wt% H2SO4 at room temperature and 900°C cyclic hot corrosion with molten salt mixtures. The regimes are different.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis focuses on a self-healing Cr2O3 passive layer on high-Cr steels. The target involves a multi-element (Al, Cr, Fe, Co) oxide/hydroxide passive layer, grain refinement, high-entropy effects, and protection against molten salt attack. The general class (passive oxide formation) overlaps, but the specific pathways and mediators differ substantially.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts lower corrosion rates for higher-Cr steels. The target predicted and reported higher microhardness, better electrochemical resistance, and lower hot-corrosion weight gain for the coated/annealed specimen. The property direction (improved corrosion resistance) is shared, but the specific metrics and comparisons differ.
